stewart_read: Customer flags wanting solar on the garage first and a future full roof replacement on the house — two live opportunities the rep let pass without acknowledgment.
coaching_implication: Rep should have flagged the future roof replacement as a bridge point for the roofing team, even briefly, per cross_sell_signals.roof_replacement_planned.

quote: Shoot. Sorry. I sent you the wrong thing.
stewart_read: Third failed bill-photo attempt; schema calls for pivoting to verbal read-back within 2 minutes of friction, not cycling repeated photo asks.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged customer was close to getting it right and stuck with photo path deliberately, but the elapsed time (multiple minutes, multiple wrong photos) argues against strategic patience.
coaching_implication: Coach the 2-minute pivot rule: after one wrong photo, switch to 'just read me the one number off the chart' verbally.

quote: The most recent one you sent, it looks like that's the daily usage.
stewart_read: Second recurrence of the same photo-mismatch friction, still not pivoted to verbal readback.
coaching_implication: This is the second touch of the same unresolved friction — should have triggered the pivot after the first miss, not the third.

quote: With the company. Yeah. So I've looked at With the company?
stewart_read: Customer references having looked at solar 'with the company' and also considering DIY, but rep doesn't probe which company or what was shown before moving to the pitch.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this detail low-value since the customer clearly wants a comparison quote anyway, but the schema calls for surfacing competitive context regardless.
coaching_implication: A quick 'which company was that, and what did they show you?' would surface competitive intel for the closer.

quote: I've always had an interest in solar, and,
stewart_read: Customer gives a rich answer mentioning an existing workshop solar system, but rep's next line is a flat acknowledgment before moving straight to address confirmation.
alternative_hypothesis: Call is a returning/high-intent lead so deep interest exploration may be less necessary than on a cold lead.
coaching_implication: Even on warm leads, reflecting the workshop-system detail back ('so you already know what solar can do for you') would have built a stronger anchor for the pitch.

quote: And, yeah, we'll give you a call Monday at 10AM.
stewart_read: Call ends with a time locked but without the schema's 'is that fair?' handshake, no-driving/computer instruction, or explicit hour-block confirmation spoken aloud in full.
coaching_implication: Add the full button-up recap (hour block, no-driving/computer ask, verbal handshake) even on a fast, cooperative close.
